assemblyC: Assembly Then C — From Zero To Good Code Path: asm first for truth (registers, stack, syscalls), then C for power. Linux x86-64, NASM + GCC + GDB . All code runnable on Debian. 0 — Setup (5 Minutes) sudo apt update && sudo apt install -y nasm gcc make gdb strace ltrace manpages-dev nasm -v; gcc --version; gdb --version # docs: https://www.nasm.us/doc/ | https://gcc.gnu.org/onlinedocs/ | https://sourceware.org/gdb/documentation/ Learn to read errors. strace ./prog shows every syscall. gdb ./prog + layout regs shows truth. 1 — Assembly Mental Model (x86-64 Linux) Registers: rax rbx rcx rdx rsi rdi rbp rsp r8-r15 (64-bit), e-kind low 32, ax/al low 16/8. Syscall ABI: rax=sysnr, rdi,rsi,rdx,r10,r8,r9=args, syscall . Syscall numbers: 0=read 1=write 60=exit (see ausyscall --dump , syscall table ). Stack grows down, rsp top, call pushes return, ret pops. 2 — First Program: exit(42) + hello ; exit42.asm — nasm -felf64 exit42.asm && ld exit42.o -o exit42; ./exit42; echo $? section .text global _start _start: mov rax, 60 ; sys_exit mov rdi, 42 syscall ; hello.asm — nasm -felf64 hello.asm && ld hello.o -o hello section .data msg db "hi from asm", 10 len equ $ - msg section .text global _start _start: mov rax, 1 ; sys_write(1, msg, len) mov rdi, 1 mov rsi, msg mov rdx, len syscall mov rax, 60 xor rdi, rdi syscall Good asm tip #1: comment every syscall with prototype. #2: xor rdi,rdi > mov rdi,0 (shorter). #3: keep .data/.bss/.text separated. 3 — Functions, Stack, Calling C Linux user calling convention (System V): args rdi,rsi,rdx,rcx,r8,r9 , return rax , callee-save rbx,rbp,r12-r15 . Align stack to 16 before call . ; strlen.asm callable from C ; nasm -felf64 strlen.asm; gcc main.c strlen.o -o main section .text global my_strlen my_strlen: ; rdi = char* xor rax, rax .loop: cmp byte [rdi+rax], 0 je .done inc rax jmp .loop .done: ret // main.c #include <stdio.h> size_t my_strlen(const char *s); int main(){ printf("%zu\n", my_strlen("hello")); } Good asm tips: frame with push rbp; mov rbp,rsp for debug, or frameless + .eh_frame for perf. Preserve callee-saved regs. Test with gdb breakpoints + info regs . 4 — C From Zero: Build Like Assembly With Types sudo apt install -y build-essential clang cppcheck valgrind gcc -std=c17 -Wall -Wextra -Werror -pedantic -g -O2 -o prog main.c # strict + debug + sanitize while learning: gcc -std=c17 -Wall -Wextra -g -O1 -fsanitize=address,undefined -o prog main.c // good.c — start here #include <stdio.h> #include <stdlib.h> int main(void){ char buf[128]; if(!fgets(buf, sizeof buf, stdin)) return 1; printf("you said: %s", buf); return 0; } Good C rule #1: -Wall -Wextra -Werror always. #2: init every variable. #3: check every return ( malloc, fopen, read ). 5 — Memory Done Right (Where C Beginners Die) // BAD: char *p = malloc(10); strcpy(p, "too long string here..."); // overflow // GOOD: #include <string.h> char *p = malloc(64); if(!p) return 1; snprintf(p, 64, "%s", input); // bounded free(p); p = NULL; char dst[32]; strncpy(dst, src, sizeof dst - 1); dst[sizeof dst - 1] = '\0'; Stack vs heap: char a[64] auto-freed, malloc manual. Strings always +1 for '\0' . Use Valgrind + ASan/UBSan until clean. Harden builds: -fstack-protector-strong -D_FORTIFY_SOURCE=2 -Wl,-z,RelRO,-z,Now -fPIE -pie , verify with checksec --file=./prog ( checksec.sh ). 6 — Good Code Habits (Asm → C Transfer) 1) Small functions, one job, early return. 2) const correctness, size_t for sizes, <stdint.h> fixed widths. 3) No magic numbers: #define BUF 128 / enum . 4) Errors as values: return -1/NULL + errno , print with perror/strerror . 5) Makefile + format ( clang-format ) + cppcheck in CI. 6) Comment why , not what — asm taught you that. CC=gcc CFLAGS=-std=c17 -Wall -Wextra -Werror -g -O2 -fstack-protector-strong -D_FORTIFY_SOURCE=2 all: prog clean:; rm -f prog *.o 7 — Debug Like A Pro gdb ./prog # b main, r, n/s, p var, bt, layout regs/src strace -f ./prog # syscalls; ltrace ./prog # lib calls valgrind --leak-check=full ./prog gcc -g -fsanitize=address,undefined ... && ./prog # fastest bug finder Reproduce tiny, then fix. One bug per commit. Write the failing test first. 8 — Where To Learn More (Curated, Free) Assembly: NASM manual , NASM tutorial (LMU) , syscall table , x86-64 syscall primer , pwn.college (asm+debug labs), 0xAX asm book . C: cppreference C , glibc manual , Beej's Guide to C , awesome-c , SEI CERT C , OWASP Secure Coding . Practice: Exercism C track , CodinGame , OverTheWire (bandit → disciplined CLI) at overthewire.org , build tiny tools: cat/clone, wc/clone, http-client . Asm shows cost. C spends it wisely. Write small, check all, sanitize always — good code is boring code that never surprises at 3am.

autonomia: Saltar para o texto Monkey Blog at odicforcesounds.com Etapa 01 / A premissa PT EN ES FR DE AR 中文 日本語 Imprimir Etapa 01 A premissa: uma ponte, não um destino Uma casa cedida a custo irrisório resolve o presente de alguém. Se ficar por aí, resolve o presente e hipoteca o futuro: cria uma dependência cómoda para quem recebe, tranquila para quem cede, e invisível para quem devia financiar a saída. O objetivo de uma cedência não é durar. É tornar-se desnecessária. Este documento parte de uma pergunta simples e desconfortável: quem ganha com o facto de esta pessoa, dentro de dois anos, já não precisar da casa cedida? A resposta inclui quase todas as instituições à volta dela — mas nenhuma é paga especificamente para isso. É por isso que a boa vontade não chega: sem protocolo, sem prazos e sem prova, o apoio transforma-se em estagnação bem-intencionada. A cedência que serve de base a esta série é o comodato solidário : o proprietário empresta o uso da casa por tempo determinado, o ocupante paga o dia a dia (consumos, condomínio, pequenas reparações) e não paga renda. Em Portugal, o comodato está nos artigos 1129.º a 1136.º do Código Civil, e o art. 1136.º coloca no comodatário as despesas ordinárias de conservação. Nada nesse contrato obriga a pessoa a trabalhar, a aceitar formação ou a agradar a quem cede — e essa liberdade é a condição de tudo o resto. A regra que organiza este documento A casa não se compra com obediência, a formação não se mede em horas e o apoio tem data. Três frases, três exigências: separação jurídica entre habitar e trabalhar; avaliação por provas e não por certificados; e critérios de saída escritos desde o primeiro dia. O que este documento não é Não é um programa de caridade, nem uma proposta para prender pessoas a casas baratas. Não é um manual de recursos humanos para empresas à procura de mão de obra barata. E não é aconselhamento jurídico: é uma proposta cívica, para ser discutida com juristas, técnicos sociais e contabilistas antes de virar regulamento. O que é: um roteiro de travessia em catorze etapas, com o mapa das instituições que têm interesse na autonomia de quem hoje vive a custo quase zero, o método para saber o que a pessoa sabe, as portas de entrada no trabalho, os limites legais que não se podem cruzar e uma forma de medir se está a funcionar. Base legal desta etapa Comodato: Código Civil, arts. 1129.º–1136.º. Despesas ordinárias: art. 1136.º. Direito à habitação: Constituição, art. 65.º. Direito ao trabalho e livre escolha de profissão: arts. 58.º e 47.º. Estes direitos não se trocam entre si — nem por contrato, nem por acordo verbal. Documento companheiro: Proposta para resolver os problemas de habitação — o modelo do comodato solidário, os custos de ceder e o catálogo de figuras legais. Etapa 02 Do modelo da casa ao modelo da economia O documento companheiro resolve a primeira metade: como ceder uma casa a custo quase zero sem que o proprietário perca o imóvel nem o ocupante perca a dignidade. Esta página resolve a segunda: como essa cedência se transforma em rendimento, qualificação e, um dia, numa casa paga a preços de mercado. Sem a primeira metade, a segunda é impossível. Sem a segunda, a primeira fica caridade permanente. Em Proposta para resolver os problemas de habitação está desenhado o instrumento: comodato com prazo, encargos separados entre quem habita e quem cede, fiscalidade que torna a cedência suportável, um catálogo de figuras legais para dar segurança jurídica e um percurso para reabilitar ruínas. O que falta é o segundo motor: transformar a margem que a casa liberta em rendimento, qualificação e património . Sem esse motor, a pessoa fica alojada e continua pobre — apenas com menos despesas. O que cada peça do modelo da casa liberta Peça O que resolve O que liberta para a economia Comodato solidário secção 3 Casa estável sem renda, com prazo certo e sem perda de propriedade. 400 a 700 €/mês de margem — o primeiro capital de arranque de quem não tinha nada. Matriz de encargos secção 3.2 Quem paga o quê: consumos e condomínio do ocupante, estrutura e IMI do proprietário, reembolsável. Elimina o conflito que faz falhar cedências e evita rendas disfarçadas. Custo corrente zero secção 6.10 O proprietário cede sem pagar para ceder. Torna o modelo repetível — sem escala, não há economia que volte. Cenários de custo secção 7.3 Mostra o que custa ceder e o que custa não ceder. Dá ao município e ao proprietário um argumento contabilístico, não moral. Guia do leitor secção 8, passo 5 O ocupante sabe exatamente o que paga e o que não paga. Confiança: quem entende o contrato investe na casa e no emprego. Catálogo de figuras legais secção 11 Usufruto, direito de superfície e habitação duradoura como alternativas ao comodato curto. Segurança de longo prazo — condição para pedir crédito e fazer obra. Ruínas para reabilitar secções 11.F e 12.3 Ativa património sem uso e entrega a casa a quem a recupera. Obra local de 400 a 1 200 €/m², com IVA, emprego próximo e casa no fim. Propostas legislativas secção 13 Isenção de IMT e Imposto do Selo na transmissão de ruínas, incentivos ao comodato. Baixa o custo de entrada e formaliza o que hoje acontece fora do contrato. A aritmética que ninguém faz Numa cidade média, uma renda de 650 € consome 72% de um salário líquido de 900 €. Com a casa cedida, esses 650 € não desaparecem: ficam disponíveis. A pergunta decisiva é o que acontece a essa margem — porque o mesmo dinheiro produz três futuros diferentes. Se a margem for consumo Cenário 1 · o mais comum O que acontece A vida melhora imediatamente e o rendimento não muda. Ao fim de cinco anos, a pessoa continua na mesma casa cedida, com a mesma taxa de esforço. Resultado Dependência confortável. Ajudou, mas não integrou. Se a margem for poupança Cenário 2 · necessário, mas insuficiente O que acontece 7 800 €/ano poupados. A entrada de 22 500 € junta-se em cerca de três anos — mas com 900 € de rendimento, a prestação continua fora de alcance. Resultado Poupança sem capacidade de crédito. A taxa de esforço não se resolve com disciplina. Se a margem for investimento Cenário 3 · o único que fecha O que acontece Parte vai para formação, transporte e creche; o resto para poupança automática. O rendimento sobe de 900 para 1 400 € e a taxa de esforço cai de 72% para 46% — e depois abaixo de 35%. Resultado Autonomia real: a casa deixa de ser necessária porque o salário passou a pagar uma. A frase que liga os dois documentos A casa barata não é o fim do problema: é o primeiro dia de um balanço . E um balanço só vale se tiver destino. Cada euro que a cedência liberta deve ter nome — formação, transporte, creche, poupança — e prazo. Sem nome, vira consumo; sem prazo, vira hábito. Há uma conclusão incômoda nesta aritmética: a poupança sozinha não compra uma casa . Para uma renda de 650 € a 35% de esforço, são precisos cerca de 1 857 € líquidos por mês. Nenhuma quantidade de disciplina fecha essa diferença — só mais rendimento, ou uma renda mais baixa, ou uma casa partilhada. É por isso que as etapas seguintes são sobre trabalho e competências, e não sobre poupança. Etapa 03 Quem tem interesse: o mapa Doze instituições têm algo a ganhar quando alguém deixa de precisar de ajuda. O truque não é convencê-las com moral: é mostrar-lhes o retorno concreto — menos emergência social, trabalhadores que ficam, alunos que terminam, clientes que pagam, reputação que se demonstra. Câmara Municipal Interesse público · habitação e coesão Ganha Menos pressão na emergência social, menos ocupação informal, novos residentes com rendimento e uma métrica que pode apresentar. Pode dar Protocolo e sala de coordenação; transporte e passe social; creche e ATL; tarifa social da água; bolsa municipal de habitação; apoio à reabilitação; sinalização de ruínas para reabilitar. Junta de Freguesia Proximidade · rede de vizinhança Ganha Conhece os casos reais, evita conflitos de vizinhança, justifica o seu papel social. Pode dar Mediação com vizinhos e senhorios, pequenas obras, lavandaria, banco de mobiliário, transporte local, ligação directa aos serviços. Pode dar Conta simplificada, microcrédito, literacia financeira, plano de poupança, simulação de crédito à habitação. Pode dar Tarifa social, planos de pagamento, equipamento eficiente, alertas de consumo, formação de literacia energética. Como se abre esta porta Não se pede a uma instituição que “ajude os pobres”. Pede-se um contributo nomeado, com prazo e com indicador : “300 horas de formação curta certificada, 12 vagas por ano”, “transporte de turno para 10 pessoas”, “cinco entrevistas garantidas por trimestre”. banthemall: Ban Them All I start using my self-hosted server. Using Linux, with tmux help, I can monitor all activity. Fail2ban is awesome to block them all. Watching before blocking The first days of a new server are the best lessons. Open a tmux session, split the window, put the web server log on one side and the packet count on the other, and the pattern appears before the coffee is cold. A handful of addresses repeat the same requests at the same rhythm. Human readers do not behave like that. tmux matters here for a boring reason: the monitoring must survive the closed terminal. A session that keeps running when the laptop lid falls is the difference between watching a log and guessing about it. How the ban actually works Fail2ban is not a firewall. It is a reader. It reads the log, matches the lines against a rule, and when an address crosses the limit it asks the firewall to drop that address for a while. That is all. No magic, no intelligence, just patience and a rule that says how many failures are allowed inside how many minutes. Two settings decide almost everything: how long the ban lasts and how wide the window is. Too short and the address returns before the lesson is learned. Too wide and an honest reader who mistyped a password three times is locked out of his own site. Ban them all, except yourself The first ban I ever made was mine. A typo, four attempts, and the server stopped answering me from my own network. Since then every configuration starts with the same line: the local addresses are always allowed. A tool that protects the door should never keep the owner outside. After that, the server became quiet. The noise is still out there, it just no longer reaches the page. That is the whole promise of a ban: not to punish anyone, only to keep the conversation small enough to be readable.

Back to the preface Level 00 / Foundation Orientation: what Bash actually is Before syntax, a mental model. Bash is not the kernel, not the terminal, and not “Linux”. It is a userland program that reads text, performs a precise sequence of expansions, and asks the kernel to run things. Almost every “weird” behaviour you will meet later is that sequence doing exactly what it was told. ~20 min no prerequisites checkpoint 4 q lab: shebang The shell is a program, not a place A terminal emulator draws a window and passes keystrokes to a program. That program is the shell : it prints a prompt, reads a line, splits it into words, expands variables and globs, then calls fork() and execve() to run the result. The kernel only sees “execute this file with these arguments”. Everything you love and hate about Bash lives in that middle layer. inspect-your-shell.sh bash copy $ echo "$SHELL" # the login shell from /etc/passwd — a claim, not a fact /bin/bash $ echo "$0" # what is running right now -bash $ ps -p $$ -o comm= # the actual executable behind this prompt bash $ command -v bash sh dash /usr/bin/bash /usr/bin/sh /usr/bin/dash $ readlink -f /usr/bin/sh /usr/bin/dash # on Debian/Ubuntu, sh is dash — not bash That last line is a career-shaping detail: #!/bin/sh does not mean “Bash with fewer features”. A very short history, and why 3.2 still matters Bash (“Bourne Again SHell”) was written by Brian Fox for the GNU Project, first released in 1989, as a free replacement for Stephen Bourne's sh . It grew into the default login shell of most Linux distributions. big_repo: Big Big Big Repository I normally like to clone some repositories to explore them at home, offline, but sometimes, some repos are bigger than I could ever Imagine. https://github.com/mthcht/awesome-lists have about 25GB :o Hopefully this repo is full of details that I will find them useful. Metadata: after removing metadata, 900MB is the real size What 25GB means for a clone A clone is not a copy of the files you see on the web page. It is a copy of the entire history, every version of every file, and every message that describes why the change happened. When a repository collects lists of links, the lists change constantly, and each change leaves a version behind. Twenty thousand small edits produce twenty thousand snapshots of the same text. That is where the size comes from, and it is also why the number felt absurd to me at first. The content I wanted was a few hundred pages of plain text. The container around it was twenty five gigabytes. The metadata is the weight Remove the history and the same repository fits in less than a gigabyte. This is the same lesson I keep finding everywhere: the useful part is small, the bookkeeping around it is enormous. File systems do the same thing, mail servers do the same thing, and any folder with a thousand small files will spend more space on the map than on the territory. It is not a defect. Metadata is what makes the data findable, comparable and recoverable. It is the reason I can ask a repository what changed last month and get an answer. But it is also the reason I check the size before I start a clone on a machine with a small disk. How I clone now A shallow clone takes the last version and leaves the history on the server. If I only want to read the lists, that is all I need, and the download becomes minutes instead of an afternoon. If I later want the history of one file, I can ask for exactly that file. I still keep the full clone of the repositories I care about, because reading old commits is the cheapest way to understand why a project is shaped the way it is. The trick is to decide before pressing enter, not after the disk is full.

bots: All Bots are welcome As you may see, this is a open source project and you can clone it and open a pull request. Sadly for your bots, I use Cloudflare, which is something that depend on them, not on me. ;) A bot is only a program with a schedule There is nothing evil in a bot. A crawler that reads this page to build an index, an archiver that keeps a copy for the future, a script that checks whether the site is still alive at three in the morning: all of those are polite, useful and welcome. They arrive once, they read, they leave, and they come back when it makes sense. The unfriendly part is never the automation, it is the control . When a thousand machines repeat the same request in the same second and none of them was invited, the site is not being read, it is being tested for weakness. The difference between a reader and an attack is not the tool, it is the intention behind the schedule. So nothing here is a secret The source of this blog is public. You can clone it, read it, fork it and open a pull request. If you find a spelling mistake, a broken link or a paragraph that makes no sense, tell me and I will be grateful. That is the whole point of working in the open: the correction is free and it arrives from someone who was paying attention. What is not public is the right to hammer the server. That decision is not mine anyway. Cloudflare decides which request is a browser and which request is a machine in a hurry, and I only see the result in the statistics. If your bot is challenged, it is not because I dislike bots, it is because the line between a crawler and a flood is thinner than it looks from the outside. What a bot can still do here Read the text. Follow the links. Take the RSS feed if you want the articles in your terminal. Keep a copy for an archive. brutalBSD: Long Life OpenBSD \./ 2026-06-07 — — OpenBSD is the system I recommend when somebody asks me which one to read before which one to install. Not because it is easy, but because the documentation is honest. A manual that explains the whole system in the order in which the system boots is worth more than a thousand tutorials written by people who copied each other. This page is a tribute and a set of notes. It is not a guide, and it will not replace man afterboot . Being paranoid about security can be a little bit Evil , but if you find that others are trying to Break it, there is no Evil on it The question is: "If you wish to break some system, which best position you should be in? Inside or Outside?" OpenBSD ask some key tips for new users, like me or like you. Always use the more option and append the number of the email, to read the emails you will get on OpenBSD system by default. Is a Golden tip. Else you will only be able to read the last lines of your emails. For the first Welcome email, you lose all the necessary details to start, while you have access to all necessary details to participate, by sending your hw.sensors values. In case you use the correct option to read your emails, you figure out that OpenBSD creates a map of necessary steps and readings to start configuring the system, much better than any other BSD or Linux System. Their Welcome email, start to explain the very basics of using the man pages in the default Kshell and ask the user to type man afterboot , to start reading the first book, of many other books that are in the same Open Library , which is always Open , at any hour of any day and any night. Then it gives an example on how to install new packages using their Binary package manager, some extra notes and we start reading book after book. Sometimes in a exaustive experience, since they always link the necessary Books that are related to the one we are reading. All makes sense and there is no Hidden or secret knowledge, like what happen with FreeBSD man pages , when I was stucked on creating a disk file to use the VMs . In the other hand, OpenBSD vm manual pages, have the option to create those disk-files and all steps that are needed are explained the best they can, since we have access to the /etc/examples/* files that are not empty. By reading the afterboot book, you can know how everything is connected, how everything should work, what limitations exist, what security problems can happen, what can you do to prevent them, how to configure each service they have that are always Open , at any time of day or night. To me as a old Linux user, I always dream about this kind of approach, where there is a guide to start, which is available offline, in the shell, trying to prevent reading external resources, that can be old and useless, with options that don't exist in the -current version, creating misconfigurations and other possible problems to those who just follow along the steps that some articles describe, while I cannot deny, many awesome articles on the web about OpenBSD that are very useful, since they connect many services running at the same time, giving us a better understanding of how many services can run at the same time in peace. man security is just one of many books, that are refered in the afterboot Book. Not like any other BSD or Linux system, OpenBSD already try to secure your system, while you can hardener a bit more, even if you can update and patch your system when bugs or security issues are found and fixed with syspatch . If you think about Linux in general, You need to spend a lot of time to secure your system, while you need to understand how to configure a secure system without creating new problems on running some service, like what can happen with SELinux by being unable to login as root when testing and learning about that tecnology that looks simple but can be damn complex too. You are using a Firewall by default. You can create all kind of network.interfaces too. All tools that I knew from Linux, I can see a simple version on OpenBSD while being more rebust. Sadly, most of my computers have a NVIDIA GPU, and OpenBSD have no support, while I am not Linux gamer. My Windows machines are always secure because they are always and always were and always be, offline . No updates to break my Windows. They are perfect like that. Offline . Because my games run offline and if you physical access to them, you can only find games. I prefere papers for sensitive data. Libraries and Offices are always better when papers exist. Is just another "non-sense" evolution where companies and individuals Expose personal data on the web. The three commands that matter in the first hour Every new installation is a small panic. These three, in this order, replace the panic with a plan: man afterboot — the map. Read it once, slowly, with the machine beside you. man security — the list of what is already protected and what is still your responsibility. syspatch — the reminder that documentation does not patch a kernel. Run it, and run it again next week. What "brutal" actually means People call the OpenBSD documentation brutal because it does not try to be friendly. It does not congratulate you for opening a terminal. It does not produce a video. It gives you a sentence, precisely written, that stays true for the next ten years, and it assumes that you are capable of reading it. That is not brutality, that is respect. The brutal thing is the other model: a documentation that changes every six months, hides the important paragraph behind a newsletter form, and calls the reader a "user" while treating him like a lead. Where the philosophy touches the hardware The same idea appears in the code. A small base system, a firewall enabled by default, privilege separation everywhere, and a maintainer culture that prefers removing a feature to auditing it forever. You can disagree with the choices and still learn from the method: decide what the system must do, remove everything else, and write down the reason. My only real complaint is the one I have repeated many times in this blog: NVIDIA. Most of my machines carry one, and OpenBSD does not support the proprietary driver, so the tribute is written from a laptop that boots something else. A system can be excellent and still not be the system for your hardware. That is a fact about my desk, not about the project. Reading before installing If this page convinces you of one thing, let it be the order: read first, install second. The library is already on the machine, waiting behind a command, and it is the only library I know that opens at three in the morning, without a connection, and without asking who you are. ↑

OdicforceSounds In English Twenty chapters Pali · Sanskrit · Chinese 學 學 How to read this manual Buddhism is not one thing. It is a family of traditions two and a half millennia old, spread from Afghanistan to Japan, written in at least six languages, and split by arguments that are still live. This manual keeps the layers apart so that the whole can be seen. The first layer is the early teaching preserved in Pali and in Chinese and Tibetan parallels: the four truths, dependent origination, the eightfold path, the discipline of the monks. The second is the Mahayana expansion, from roughly the first century BCE: the bodhisattva ideal, emptiness, buddha-nature, vast sutras and a cosmos full of Buddhas. The third is the tantric or Vajrayana layer from the sixth century CE onward: initiation, deity yoga, mandala and mantra, in Tibet, Japan and parts of China. The fourth is the modern layer: colonial scholarship, Theosophy, the mindfulness industry, secular Buddhism. Two rules First: a text's age is not its authority. The Pali canon is older than the Lotus Sutra; that makes it earlier, not truer. Second: the tradition itself knows its texts were composed over centuries, and has its own explanation — upāya , skilful means, and the idea that a Buddha teaches what a given audience can hear. Languages matter. Pali is the Middle Indo-Aryan language of the Theravada canon; Sanskrit is the cosmopolitan language of the Mahayana and the tantras; Chinese and Tibetan are the two great translation canons; Japanese and Korean carry their own transmissions. A term like dukkha appears in this manual with its Pali form, and Sanskrit equivalents where they differ ( duḥkha in Sanskrit, 苦 in Chinese). This is a descriptive manual. It is not a creed, not an initiation, and not medical or psychological advice. Where the tradition makes empirical claims — about rebirth, about the effects of meditation, about the cosmos — the text says what is claimed and what can be checked. The reader is trusted with the difference. One thread connects this manual to the rest of the site: the Buddhist Monkey . The Monkey King Sun Wukong is a Buddhist literary figure — the pilgrim who escorts Xuanzang west to fetch sutras in Journey to the West — and OdicforceSounds has long used the Monkey as the figure of a mind that cannot sit still. That monkey is the reader of this manual: curious, impatient, and occasionally enlightened by accident. 佛 佛 The Buddha and the story 佛陀 fótuó is not a name but a title: buddha , "one who has awakened". The historical teacher was Siddhattha Gotama in Pali, Siddhārtha Gautama in Sanskrit, of the Sakya clan — which is why he is called Sakyamuni , the sage of the Sakyas. The dates are disputed. The tradition's long chronology puts him at 563–483 BCE; most modern scholars prefer something like 480–400 BCE, with the death somewhere near 400. He was born at Lumbini, in what is now Nepal, raised at Kapilavatthu, and, according to the story, kept inside a palace by a father who wanted him to be a king rather than a renunciant. The four sights The story turns on a chariot ride. Sheltered prince meets, in succession, an old man, a sick man, a corpse, and a wandering ascetic who looks at ease. The first three teach him that the body is a loan; the fourth shows a way of living with that knowledge. He leaves the palace, studies with two teachers of absorption, masters their attainments, finds them insufficient, and spends years in extreme austerity until he is nearly dead. Then a memory — as a boy, under a rose-apple tree, he had entered a natural state of calm — suggests that the body is not the enemy. He takes food, sits under a pipal tree at Bodh Gaya, and resolves not to rise until he understands. The night is described as a battle with Māra, the tempter and lord of the sense-realm: armies, daughters, the offer of a kingdom. He touches the earth as witness, and by dawn he is awake. What "awake" means here Not omniscience about everything, but the end of the three fermentations: sensual desire, becoming, and ignorance. The traditional formula is that he knew suffering, its arising, its cessation, and the path — which is to say, the four truths, seen not as propositions but as tasks completed. He teaches for about forty-five years. The first sermon, at the deer park at Sarnath, is the Dhammacakkappavattana Sutta , "the turning of the wheel of dharma": the middle way, the four truths, the eightfold path. His last words, in the Mahāparinibbāna Sutta , are a warning against relying on a person: Mahāparinibbāna Sutta · Pali “Handa dāni, bhikkhave, āmantayāmi vo: vayadhammā saṅkhārā, appamādena sampādetha.” “Come now, monks, I address you: all conditioned things decay. Strive on with diligence.” Dīgha Nikāya 16 He is not a god in the early texts, and he discourages a cult of his person. Asked what should happen after his death, he says: do not worry about the funeral, practise. The relics and the stupa come later, and become one of the great engines of the tradition. Buddhas before and after The early texts already have previous Buddhas — Vipassī, Sikhī, Vessabhū, Kakusandha, Koṇāgamana, Kassapa — and a future one, Metteyya (Maitreya), who waits in the Tuṣita heaven. The pattern matters more than the names: awakening is not a one-off event in history but a recurring possibility, and the dharma is rediscovered each time it is lost. The biographical genre grows enormously. The Buddhacarita of Aśvaghoṣa (2nd century CE) is a Sanskrit epic; the Pali Jātaka tales give hundreds of previous lives; the Lalitavistara adds the miracles. The story as most of Asia knows it is a composite, and it is meant to be contemplated, not fact-checked like a newspaper. 若見諸相非相，即見如來 If you see all appearances as no-appearance, you see the Tathāgata. Diamond Sutra, chapter 5 諦 四諦 Four truths, eight steps The four noble truths are not a creed but a diagnosis, and the tradition often points out that they follow the shape of Indian medicine: the disease, its cause, the possibility of cure, the treatment. 四聖諦 — the four noble truths, with the task each assigns Truth Pali Content Task 苦 dukkha suffering, unsatisfactoriness, the friction of conditioned existence to be understood 集 samudaya craving ( taṇhā ) — for pleasure, for becoming, for non-becoming to be abandoned 滅 nirodha the ending of craving, and therefore of the whole mass of suffering to be realised 道 magga the eightfold path, the middle way between indulgence and mortification to be developed Dukkha is famously hard to translate: "suffering" is too dark, "stress" too mild, "unsatisfactoriness" accurate but clumsy. The image is a wheel whose axle does not fit — duḥ , bad, plus kha , the hole. Even pleasure is dukkha in the sense that it cannot last and leaves a hunger behind it. The eightfold path The path is usually grouped into three trainings — ethics ( sīla ), concentration ( samādhi ) and wisdom ( paññā ) — and the order is a spiral rather than a ladder: right view guides the rest, and the rest clarifies right view. 八正道 — the noble eightfold path Factor Pali What it means in practice 正見 sammā-diṭṭhi seeing the four truths, karma and impermanence as they apply to this life 正思惟 sammā-saṅkappa intention free of sensuality, ill will and cruelty 正語 sammā-vācā no lying, divisive speech, harsh speech or idle chatter 正業 sammā-kammanta no killing, stealing or sexual misconduct 正命 sammā-ājīva a livelihood that does not require harming others 正精進 sammā-vāyāma cultivating good states and abandoning unwholesome ones 正念 sammā-sati mindfulness of body, feeling, mind and phenomena 正定 sammā-samādhi the four absorptions ( jhāna ), unified and translucent Two parables keep the path from becoming an ideology. The raft : the dharma is a raft for crossing, not a possession to carry on your head — even the teaching is to be let go when it has done its work. The arrow : a man shot by an arrow refuses treatment until he knows the archer's name, clan, height and the kind of bow; he dies before the answers arrive. The unanswered metaphysical questions ( avyākata ) — is the world eternal? is it finite? is the self the body? — are set aside not because they are forbidden but because they do not help with the arrow. 諸惡莫作，眾善奉行，自淨其意，是諸佛教 Not doing any evil, undertaking the good, purifying one's mind — this is the teaching of the Buddhas. Dhammapada 183 緣 緣起 Impermanence, no-self, karma Three observations are said to cover all conditioned things: anicca , they change; dukkha , they cannot satisfy; anattā , they are not a self. The third is the one Western readers find hardest, and the one the tradition insists on. The five aggregates What we call "I" is analysed into five heaps — not parts of a self, but processes that a self is imputed to: rūpa — form, the body and the material world. vedanā — feeling-tone: pleasant, unpleasant, neutral. saññā — perception, the labelling that recognises. saṅkhārā — formations: volition, habit, the constructing mind. viññāṇa — consciousness, the knowing of each sense door. The argument is not "there is no person". It is that nothing in the heap is permanent, and nothing in it is ownerless of change, so nothing in it deserves the name "self" in the sense of an unchanging essence. The person remains — as a process, a stream, a convention. Dependent origination 緣起 paṭicca-samuppāda is the central doctrine, older in feel than the four truths and arguably deeper: when this is, that is; with the arising of this, that arises. L0 L0 — What “capitalism” technically is PREREQ: NONE · OBJECTIVE: DEFINE THE 5 PILLARS · TIME 15 MIN 0.1 Definition without slogans Capitalism is a coordination system where (1) most productive assets are privately owned , (2) production is guided by prices formed in markets , (3) investment comes from accumulated capital seeking return , (4) labour is hired via wage contracts , and (5) firms compete under (imperfect) rule of law . Remove any pillar and you get a different system (see L6). Capital Wealth set aside to produce more wealth: machines, stock, cash, code, reputation. Market Any protocol where buyers/sellers meet and a price clears (bazaar, NYSE, eBay, Uber surge). Profit Revenue − full costs. Signal that says “do more of this” (or “stop”). Competition Rivalry that copies success and punishes waste — when entry is actually open. 0.2 Animated: the circular flow FIG 0-A · HOUSEHOLDS ⇄ FIRMS (ANIMATED) Households → labour → Firms → wages → Households → spending → Firms … Households sell labour/capital; firms pay wages/interest/dividends; households buy goods; money loops. Leaks: savings, taxes, imports. Injections: investment, state spending, exports. 0.3 Why prices matter (the information argument) Economist F. Hayek’s point: no planner knows everyone’s needs. A rising bread price compresses thousands of facts (bad harvest + fuel cost + demand) into one number everyone can act on. That is powerful — and also brutal, because price alone ignores who can pay.
